title: Resolved font recipe options
description: What `mdux-textbake` was asked to do when baking a font package: the source face, the pixel size it was rasterised at, the locales it approves, and the restricted charset it admits. Describes the **resolved** option set a baker records in `report.json`'s `options`, with every default expanded - not the literal TOML a recipe file carries. ADR-007 decision 4 is why: a silently changed default must not leave every report looking unchanged, so the report records what the bake actually did, and this documents that. Checked against every committed report by tools/docs-lint/check_schema_type_drift.py.

id.description: The artifact id, which names the directory under `generated/font/`.

source.description: Repository-relative path to the source face the atlas was rasterised from.

atlas.description: Always the empty string for a font recipe, and required because it is always present. `mdux-textbake` bakes both kinds from one `Recipe`, whose `atlas` member is a *text* recipe's - the id of the font package its runs index glyphs in - and the shared prefix of `toOptions()` emits it before the kind branch. A font package is not positioned against an atlas; it is one. The member is emitted unconditionally rather than omitted so that font and text reports have one shape, which is the same reason `font` and `strings` are always present on a text report. Where the atlas bytes go is `sidecar`.

sidecar.description: The file the R8 coverage atlas is written to, beside `package.json`.

pixelSize.description: The pixel size every glyph was rasterised at. There is one size per package: ADR-010 keeps run-time scaling out, so a second size is a second package.

locale.description: The locale the package is primarily baked for.

items.description: A BCP 47 tag this font approves.

locales.description: Every locale the package approves. A screen recipe must name one committed text package per entry here - a locale approved with no package is a build error, because a budget checked against fewer locales than were approved is a claim nobody made.

charset.description: The restricted charset the atlas admits, as closed code-point ranges. A character outside it has no glyph, which is what bounds what any screen using this font can display.

name.description: The range's name in the recipe.
